statement: POST /users/:id/deactivate exists and is permission-gated on the server, but no admin surface calls it; the UI deactivates through PATCH /users/:id instead, so one action has two server paths and one of them is dead code with its own audit action (user.deactivate).

statement: GET /users/:id is permission-gated and returns a full user view (roles with names, locale), but the admin app never calls it: there is no user detail route, and the only admin callers of /users are the list, the roles list, invite and PATCH. A capability that exists server-side has no affordance, so the list row is the only surface.

`locale` is part of the users API contract (selected in list and detail) and is required by the admin's response schema, but it is rendered nowhere and cannot be edited from the panel: a contract field with no UI surface and no affordance saying where it lives.

The invite form's name and email inputs carry no autocomplete token, so user information cannot be filled from the browser's own data; the same app's registration wizard sets autoComplete="email" on its email field, so the convention exists and this form deviates from it. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.5 (AA) names this as identifying input purpose.

where: users list vs the app's list convention
statement: The users page fetches every user and filters in memory, while the API family's contract is cursor pagination and the sibling list pages implement it; the users service even returns a page envelope with nextCursor:null and hasNextPage:false hardcoded, so the envelope asserts something the server never computed. The list therefore cannot scale, and search covers only the records already fetched.

Search is a plain GET input plus a submit button: no typeahead or suggestion dropdown, no server-side search, substring match over displayName+email only (Turkish lowercasing, no diacritic folding, so 'sukru' does not find 'Şükrü'), and the result count is written into a plain paragraph with no live region, so a screen reader is told nothing when the filter changes.

The picker's results are a separate native select, not a combobox: the search input has no role=combobox, no aria-expanded, no aria-activedescendant, no listbox popup and no arrow-key navigation, and the status node never announces how many results arrived (only 'Aranıyor…', an error, or a constant sentence). The WAI-ARIA APG combobox pattern is not met, and assistive technology cannot discover that a result list exists.

When the customer select changes, the equipment picker silently empties both its result list and its selection by resetting React state; the field announces nothing (the status node keeps whatever text it had), no dependent validation is re-run, and nothing tells the user a value they had chosen was discarded. The cascade is a data-losing action with no message.

The three-step registration flow does enforce its prerequisites on the server: a request for a step whose precondition is unmet is redirected to the resume step, and a submitted application is pinned to the last step. The check that must not be skipped is genuinely enforced, so this row records a covered case rather than a defect.

Step 1 collects service categories as one free-text comma-separated input with only 'non-empty' required, while step 2 requires exactly three READY documents and gates step 3 on that count. The two steps disagree on how structured their input is: the wizard validates a count it can compute and accepts a string it cannot, so a typo'd or empty category list passes the gate that exists for it.

One entity's edit is split across three surfaces with no map between them: invite (create), the row modal (role/scope/active only, by design), and self-service for name and language. The row modal's only hint is the sentence in its description, and the API's own error GLOBAL_PROFILE_SELF_SERVICE_REQUIRED is never surfaced as guidance. A detail page per user, which the existing GET /users/:id would support, is never proposed.

The invite dialog offers no draft/autosave, no inline duplicate-email check (ALREADY_MEMBER arrives only after a submit round trip) and preselects a role when TECHNICIAN is assignable; that default grants an access scope the user never chose and is not called out as a default in the form copy.

Changing a role replaces every existing role, and the copy says so, but the confirmation dialog lists only the new values ('Yeni rol', 'Kapsam', 'Üyelik'), never the roles about to be removed. The person confirming a destructive change cannot see what is lost, which is the one fact the confirmation exists to show.

None of D01-D13 can be repaired inside the screen: the fixes are a server-side search and paginated users list, a user detail aggregate, an autocomplete convention in the form components, a combobox primitive in the design system, and an inline uniqueness check. The artifact the analysis is required to produce has no section in which an infrastructure change is proposed, so a run has nowhere to put this class of finding and reports UI copy instead.
